source_items.source_provenance: Synthetic Core2 golden QG-PHY-01; process fixture only.

source_body.stem: A projectile has vertical velocity 12 m/s upward at t = 1 s. Take g = 10 m/s^2. What was its initial vertical velocity?

figure_semantics: one global time axis from launch to the stated event
core2_representation.first_step_reference: Place the stated event on the clock that started at launch.

hints.text: The stated time is measured from launch; gravity has acted for the full interval.
Use the vertical constant-acceleration velocity model with upward positive.
Write v_y = u_y - gt and isolate the launch component.

representation_stages: mark launch at t=0 and the known event at t=1 s
show downward acceleration while vertical velocity remains upward
solution: Use v_y = u_y - gt at t=1 s.
verification: After one second, gravity should have reduced the upward vertical velocity by 10 m/s.

challenge_candidates.prompt: During a projectile flight the vertical component is 6 m/s upward at t = 2 s. With upward positive and g = 9 m/s^2, determine the launch vertical component.

staged_help.small_clue: Keep one clock from launch to the stated event.
staged_help.bigger_clue: Use the signed vertical velocity relation for constant downward acceleration.
staged_help.how_do_i_start: Substitute the known later vertical velocity and elapsed time before rearranging.

full_working: Take upward as positive, so a_y = -9 m/s^2.
Use v_y = u_y + a_y t: 6 = u_y - 18.
quick_check: Over 2 s, gravity changes vertical velocity by 18 m/s downward; 24 - 18 = 6 m/s.

challenge_candidates.prompt: A projectile is launched with vertical component 30 m/s. Its vertical component later becomes 3 m/s upward. If the vertical acceleration is -9 m/s^2, find how long after launch this state occurs.

staged_help.small_clue: The target is now the event time rather than a velocity.
staged_help.bigger_clue: Keep the same signed constant-acceleration relation.
staged_help.how_do_i_start: Put the launch and later vertical components into v_y = u_y + a_y t, then isolate t.

quick_check: In 3 s the vertical component drops by 27 m/s, from 30 m/s to 3 m/s.
